newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia to ask IMF time for changes in monopolies.
newsitem.headline: Russia to ask IMF time for changes in monopolies.

text.p: Russia will ask the International Monetary Fund (IMF) for a respite of several months to decide how to restructure its natural monopolies, First Deputy Prime Minister Vladimir Potanin was quoted as saying on Thursday.

"We accept the obligation to set up competition in the area of natural monopolies, but we shall make it clear how to implement it in the next few months," Prime-Tass news agency quoted Potanin as saying.
Natural gas producer Gazprom, national power grid operator Unified Energy System (UES) and the railways are Russia's main natural monopolies.
Potanin said UES and Gazprom agreed with the government's position, Prime-Tass said.
He said the Economy Ministry and the Fuel and Energy Ministries had different opinions on how natural monopolies should be restructured.

The Economy Ministry agree with the IMF that Russia should remove power-generating companies from UES's structure, but UES and the Fuel and Energy Ministry think this is not necessary, since there are already independent power-generating companies in existence, Prime-Tass said.
Potanin said the government could try to separate Gazprom's production units from its distribution system.
"Gas production is so much monopolised that we have to shake it up," he said.
President Boris Yeltsin told parliament on Thursday that natural monopoly prices were unjustifiably high, fuelling a non-payments crisis.
Potanin said Gazprom did not object to changes in its price policy, Prime-Tass said.
